quote.text: September is a second spring when every leaf is a flower.
quote.author: Albert Camus

fun_fact.text: In Hungary, September 1st traditionally marks the beginning of the school year, called "Tanévnyitó" (opening of the school year). Children often bring flowers to their teachers on this day, and it's considered a fresh start full of possibilities and new learning adventures.

short_read.title: How Hummingbirds Are Nature's Tiny Acrobats
short_read.teaser: These remarkable birds can fly backwards, upside down, and hover in place — the only birds that can do all three. Learn about the incredible flight mechanics that make hummingbirds such amazing aerial performers.

medium_read.title: The Secret Lives of Mosses in the Pacific Northwest
medium_read.teaser: The lush forests of the Olympic Peninsula are carpeted with hundreds of species of moss, each with its own story. This gentle exploration reveals how these ancient plants create miniature worlds and support entire ecosystems.

long_read.title: The Silk Road: Ancient Highway of Culture and Commerce
long_read.teaser: For thousands of years, the Silk Road connected East and West, carrying not just silk but ideas, art, and innovations across continents. This fascinating journey traces the routes that brought together diverse cultures and changed the world.

port_angeles.title: Bald Eagles Gather for Salmon Season
port_angeles.description: September marks the beginning of salmon spawning season in the Elwha River, and bald eagles from across the region gather to feast. You might spot dozens of these magnificent birds perched in trees along the river, waiting for their next meal — one of nature's most impressive spectacles right in our backyard.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart can beat up to ___ times per minute during flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right! That tiny heart works incredibly hard — faster than almost any other animal on Earth!
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute when flying — that's 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: It's actually about 1,200 beats per minute! That's faster than you can count, powering those amazing wings that beat up to 80 times per second.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To fuel this incredible metabolism, hummingbirds must eat about half their body weight in sugar each day, visiting hundreds of flowers. Their heart rate can slow to 250 beats per minute when they rest at night.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Pillangó is such a beautiful, delicate-sounding word for such a beautiful, delicate creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound lovely? (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language, part of the Finno-Ugric family, which makes it quite different from neighboring European languages. Many Hungarian words have a musical, flowing quality that reflects the culture's love of poetry and song.

puzzle_3.question: What is the name of the strait of water visible from Port Angeles?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! The Strait of Juan de Fuca is our beautiful waterway, named after a Greek explorer who sailed for Spain in 1592. On clear days, you can see Vancouver Island across the water!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's the Strait of Juan de Fuca! This beautiful waterway separates the Olympic Peninsula from Vancouver Island and connects the Pacific Ocean to Puget Sound. It was named after a Greek explorer sailing for Spain.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Strait is about 96 miles long and provides critical habitat for orcas, gray whales, seals, and countless seabirds. The waters here are some of the richest marine ecosystems in the world.
